incidents.summary: As of early September 2026, the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 6,000 confirmed cases and 3,000 deaths, with the most recent data showing 6,342 cases and 3,072 deaths as of September 2. The UK announced it will nearly triple its funding to £78.7 million, while the WHO rejected wide rollout of the Ervebo vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain and stated that trials of three potential vaccines are imminent. The DRC also launched an updated 180-day response plan seeking Sh173 billion in funding, even as the UN warns that ongoing violence and mass displacement in eastern DRC continue to undermine containment efforts.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

news.headline: Médecins Sans Frontières Launches 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition to Spotlight Humanitarian Crises and Ebola Disease Outbreak in DRC
news.body: HONG KONG, July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Hong Kong yesterday held an opening ceremony for its 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition. As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

incidents.summary: Multiple UN agencies and scientific reports now classify the 2026-27 El Niño as "supersized," potentially the strongest in a millennium, warning it will persist until early 2027 and intensify droughts, floods, and extreme heat worldwide. Regionally, South Florida exited extreme drought after recent rains, while Karnataka, India launched a $28.5 million cloud seeding project, and the USDA designated five Montana counties as drought disaster areas. Droughts worsened in Arkansas, North Carolina, and Sri Lanka, and Colorado reported a massive increase in bear-human incidents due to dry conditions.

logs.summary:
New reports confirm the UK experienced its hottest summer on record since 1884, with temperatures averaging 16.8°C, exacerbating drought conditions. South Africa faces a hotter, drier summer as a "very strong" El Niño develops, while Indonesia warns of challenging wildfire containment as the El Niño peaks this month. In the US, Puerto Rico's drought intensifies prompting a federal water disaster declaration, Lakeland Florida considers $500 fines for repeat water violations amid persistent drought, and Colorado Springs recorded near-record August heat and drought, with the month being the fourth-warmest on record.
New reports detail economic impacts: France expects drought and heatwaves to shave 0.1% off 2026 GDP, while British farmers face cumulative losses of nearly £5 billion from three weather-hit harvests (2024–2026). South Africa's weather service warns of a potentially record-strength El Niño bringing below-normal rainfall and hotter, drier spring conditions, and East Africa sees a moderate to strong El Niño settling with a 2.9°C sea-surface anomaly. Locally, drought persists in Mississippi amid heat advisories, and Ireland's Co Carlow ended a 66-day partial drought.

logs.summary: New reports warn of a potentially record-strength "super El Niño" that could intensify global drought, with South Africa's weather service saying it may be the strongest in living memory and the WMO confirming a "very strong" event. In the US, New Mexico's Elephant Butte Reservoir plummeted to just 1.4% capacity, drought deepened in northern Mississippi and northwest Wisconsin, and Colorado's Vail Duck Race was forced to move from creek to land due to unprecedented low flows. Meanwhile, Indonesia's peatlands are burning as drought grips the region, and the UK confirmed summer 2026 as its hottest on record, with scientists warning such extreme heat may return every nine years.

logs.summary:
Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

logs.summary:
Russia struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea, escalating maritime attacks, while Putin cited a chance for a peace deal and Ukraine noted a "new dynamic" in peace efforts. India's foreign minister visited Kyiv offering diplomatic help, and Ukraine formally warned international aviation that Russian airspace is unsafe, broadening the air war. Russia's oil revenue hit a six-month low as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to pressure the economy, and strikes near Moldova raised fears of escalation beyond Ukraine.

logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
Renewed hostilities saw Iran fire missiles and drones at Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for U.S. airstrikes that Iran claims killed 18 people, including civilians at a wedding, while Trump administration officials publicly contradicted each other—Commerce Secretary Lutnick falsely stated no American deaths occurred and later apologized—and observers reported the conflict has reached a stalemate with no end in sight. Trump is reportedly weighing a formal declaration of victory to end the war even as the Pentagon extends troop deployments into 2027, and conservatives urged him to issue such a declaration amid mounting political and economic pressures.
On September 3, Vice President JD Vance told a White House press briefing that the Iran conflict is "not a war" and declined to offer an end timeline, drawing sharp criticism and contradictions with prior administration statements. Iran retaliated against fresh U.S. strikes by targeting Kuwait and the UAE, while oil prices surged and U.S. diesel prices hit a record high of $5.85 per gallon. Reports indicate Trump is privately weighing a declaration that the conflict is over, even as Republicans acknowledge the war will last past the November midterm elections.

news.headline: US-Iran War Live: US, allies draft resolution to refer Iran to UN Security Council
news.body: US-Iran War Live: President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that the United States may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain very soon. He also accused Democrats of preferring a US defeat in the Iran conflict over a White House victory as Republicans face November midterm elections amid rising food and fuel prices. Meanwhile, the US, Britain, France and Germany are pushing an IAEA resolution to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over alleged nuclear violations. The development comes as US Vice President JD Vance said Washington was investigating reports that a US airstrike in southern Iran hit a wedding party, reportedly killing five people and wounding nearly 70. Vance said the US cared about the reports and wanted to establish the facts. He declined to set a timeline for ending the conflict and ruled out talks while Iran targeted commercial shipping. Follow indiatoday.in for the latest updates on the US-Iran war.

logs.summary: Massive wildfires in southwest France and Spain have forced hundreds of thousands of evacuations, with the blaze near Bordeaux growing so intense it generated lightning that ignited new fires. French President Macron pledged support on a visit to the fire zone, while officials reported that the fire has stabilized but is not yet contained. Two firefighters died battling the flames in a Bordeaux suburb.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

news.headline: Europe Battles Extreme Weather: France, Spain, Serbia & Bosnia Hit By Wildfires, Floods And Storms
news.body: Extreme weather is gripping multiple European nations as severe wildfires, flash floods and powerful storms force thousands of people to evacuate. France is battling a major wildfire across the Cap Ferret Peninsula in the southwest, where extreme summer heat and months of drought have created dangerous fire conditions. Authorities ordered the evacuation of the popular tourism hotspot as flames threatened homes and the peninsula’s main escape route. More than 10,000 hectares of forest have reportedly been affected, while around 63,000 people, including large numbers of tourists, were forced to leave the area. Boats and emergency teams were deployed as authorities worked to protect residents and visitors. Spain is also facing a contrasting weather crisis, with intense wildfires occurring alongside torrential rainfall and flash flooding. Heavy rains disrupted road and rail transport and injured more than 11 people.

logs.summary: In early August 2026, wildfires in western Canada, particularly the Bald Range fire near Summerland, British Columbia, escalated dramatically. The fire burned over 33,000 acres, destroyed approximately 230 homes, and resulted in the death of one woman, prompting evacuation orders for around 20,000 people. In response, British Columbia declared a state of emergency as crews faced challenging conditions from severe drought and windy weather.

news.headline: Varanasi Floods: PM Reviews Relief Operations as Ganga Water Crosses Warning Mark
news.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to the Mayor and Collector of Varanasi to review the flood situation in the constituency. The Prime Minister was briefed on ongoing relief measures and directed the local administration to ensure citizens face minimal inconvenience and work on a war footing. Continuous rainfall has pushed up the water levels of the river Ganga, breaching the warning mark and submerging pedestrian paths and the famed ghats along the riverbank. Authorities have suspended boat operations in the city, while displaced residents are being moved into relief camps with arrangements for food and drinking water.

logs.summary: Severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and flash flooding impacted multiple regions across the United States from August 20–24, 2026. Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

news.headline: Severe thunderstorm watch issued for west-central Saskatchewan
news.body: Environment Canada has issued a severe thunderstorm watch for west-central Saskatchewan as conditions become favourable for storms capable of producing strong wind gusts, large hail and heavy rain. The watch was issued at 3:03 p.m. Friday and carries a moderate impact level with high forecast confidence. Environment Canada says a trough of low pressure moving across southwestern Saskatchewan is expected to trigger thunderstorms late Friday afternoon and into the evening. Some of those storms could become severe. logs.summary: A large wildfire ignited in the High Fens nature reserve in eastern Belgium (Liège province) around August 14, 2026, destroying approximately 3,000 hectares (12 square miles) of land. Firefighters from Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands battled the blaze, which threatened to spread into Germany and prompted partial evacuations in the border town of Monschau. Rain on August 17 brought some relief, slowing the fire's advance towards the German border.

news.headline: Wildfires expose — and detonate — buried bombs and mines from WWI and WWII
news.body: ELSENBORN, Belgium (AP) — The wildfires burning across Europe this summer have exposed a potentially deadly threat lurking beneath the blackened landscape: rusty bombs and mines from World War I and II that threaten crews responding to the flames. Some of the weapons have exploded in the intense heat. Blasts have been reported in France, […]

incidents.summary: As of September 3, 2026, the death toll from the M7.7 earthquake in East Nusa Tenggara has risen to 127, according to BNPB. Meanwhile, the Indonesian Church is training volunteers for response efforts in Flores, and fact-checkers debunked a viral video falsely claiming that cash linked to a politician was found in the earthquake rubble.

logs.summary:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

logs.summary: A glacier collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides on August 26, 2026, sweeping through several communities in the Bagmati region. The disaster has killed hundreds of people (with death tolls reported between 350 and 500) and left over 1,300 missing, including dozens of foreign nationals. Rescue teams are searching for survivors while authorities warn of additional flood risks from a newly formed lake, and international aid is arriving to support relief efforts.

news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

news.headline: Nepal Flood Devastation: How Turquoise Miracle House in Chaurasi Survived
news.body: Amid massive flood devastation across Nepal, a turquoise house in Chaurasi has gained attention as Nepal's Miracle House after remaining standing while surrounding structures were swept away by raging floodwaters and debris. The building's survival is attributed to its reinforced concrete frame with concrete columns, beams, and steel reinforcement acting as an internal skeleton. This structural system provided resistance against powerful lateral forces, compression, tension, and bending caused by fast-moving water. Additionally, the house was situated slightly outside the direct path of the most destructive debris flow, allowing floodwaters to split around the building.

news.body: Catastrophic flash floods in Nepal have left more than 1,200 people dead, over 4,200 missing, and nearly 12,000 rescued. Addressing Parliament, the Prime Minister stated that Nepal never refused international assistance and thanked India and China for stepping up with rescue and relief operations. Search teams continue operations inside hydropower tunnels as recovery efforts begin. Ground reports reveal complete devastation in Betrawati, the largest town at the foothills of Rasuwa, which was swept away after a glacial collapse. The Trishuli river expanded from a 30-metre stream to over 600 metres, washing away houses, schools, temples, and bridges. Meanwhile, visuals from Dhunge Bazaar show certain structures surviving despite being submerged in 12 to 15 feet of mud, while surrounding areas were destroyed.

logs.summary:
As of September 3-4, the death toll has risen to at least 1,259 in Nepal (1,280 including Tibet), with the missing figure jumping to over 5,000. Rescuers are searching an underground room where 46 workers may survive, while Nepal weighs relocating survivors and launches a tourism campaign to counter cancellations. Warnings about glacier instability on the Tibetan Plateau and a magnitude 5.0 earthquake in Tibet add to ongoing concerns, while misinformation including AI-generated images circulates online.
On September 4, rescuers pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel nine days after the flash floods, with rescuers hearing additional voices indicating more possible survivors. The UN launched a $49.6 million flash appeal to aid over 84,000 affected people, while Nepal's disaster authority revised damage estimates to $2.56 billion, and insurers estimated commercial losses exceeding $130 million. Meanwhile, a U.S.-based Nepali fundraiser and new reports of missing foreign nationals (e.g., a Filipino doctor) continued to emerge.

logs.summary:
On September 3, 2026, two Palestinian teens were killed in the occupied West Bank as Israeli settlers and snipers surrounded a village. Israeli forces bulldozed olive trees in the West Bank, while Prime Minister Netanyahu signaled plans to expand Israeli control over Gaza and the defence minister stated Israel still wants to remove Palestinians from Gaza. Additionally, a Gaza doctor continues to suffer torture in Israeli prison, and broader regional tensions escalated with Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting Kuwait.
On September 4, 2026, the UN raised 'ethnic cleansing' concerns over Israel's West Bank operation, reporting over 33,000 Palestinian refugees still displaced. Israeli police killed a Palestinian in Jerusalem after an alleged knife attack. Meanwhile, far-right minister Ben-Gvir outlined a plan for the forced expulsion of all Palestinians from Gaza.
